driver: tokenomics.train.orderer_improve --product-stream --stochastic (M2 expert iteration; product-stream obs v3, ADR-0052; learned per-dim log_std + sampled deploy; producer fixed v4)
question: EXP-0006B promoted a stochastic orderer on the source-keyed enriched obs (v2). ADR-0052 refactors ordering agents to one per (source, product) stream and serves a dedicated product_stream obs (v3) whose width scales with producers, not the product vocabulary, and carries no product id/one-hot. Does re-distilling the stochastic orderer on the v3 product-stream contract preserve (or beat) the EXP-0006B champion on held-out seeds 6,7,8,9 with zero death — i.e. is the simpler, relabel-invariant representation at least behaviour-neutral before EXP-0007B automation targets it?

params.ordering_agents: one per (source, product) stream (ADR-0052); phase1->scale yields restricted coverage (consumer pool + producer replenishment/restoration/upgrade/inventory inputs)
params.search_teacher: directed routing search, lookahead=12, K(samples)=12, candidates {even_split, proportional, obs_price}
params.loss: masked Gaussian NLL over decode-active orderer dims (fits mean + per-dim log_std); masked dims keep init
params.deploy: sample a ~ Normal(mean, exp(log_std)), clip to +/-bound; per-episode RNG = env.action_space(agent).np_random
params.control: identical recipe to EXP-0006B except orderer_obs_version 2 (source-keyed enriched) -> orderer_obs_version 3 (product-stream, ADR-0052); action contract (k x P logits + eligibility mask) unchanged

configs.topologies: tokenomics.eval.scale.build_scale_config(seed, depth=3) — same fixed scale suite as EXP-0004/0005/0006A/0006B
configs.observation: docs/adr/0052-stable-product-stream-ordering-agents.md (product_stream_v1 = orderer_obs_version 3): product features (9, no id/one-hot) + K backlog slots (9 each) + P producer rows (31 each) + cycle progress; width independent of product count

verdict: ACCEPT (behaviour-neutral-or-better). Authoritative numbers are the corrected STREAM-layout re-eval (review P2 fix: bars scored in the candidate's agent layout, not legacy — `random` consumes action-space RNG over the stream-keyed agent set). Re-distilling the stochastic orderer on the v3 product-stream contract clears the strict random-inclusive envelope on ALL held-out seeds 6,7,8,9 (own-layout env-ratio 1.045/1.086/1.056/1.038 @10 eval seeds), zero death. Vs the EXP-0006B v2 champion's own-layout ratios (1.026/1.086/1.057/1.022): v3 >= v2 on s6 (1.045>1.026) and s9 (1.038>1.022, the historically hard seed), tied on s7 (1.086) and s8 (1.056 vs 1.057). Mean env-ratio 1.056 (v2 1.048; both < secondary 1.10). The simpler, relabel-invariant, product-count-independent representation clears the strict envelope everywhere with zero death -> safe to make the EXP-0007B automation target. NOTE: cross-experiment absolute units are not directly comparable (cloud-vs-local domain float drift, ~0.1%, flips borderline auction acceptances); deterministic-baseline parity is bit-identical legacy-vs-stream at depth-3 scale (0 episode mismatches). Checkpoint v3 fp distinct from v1/v2; 32 focused tests green incl. 2 P2 regression guards. m2_stream_stochastic.pt.

gates.primary: M2-stream-stochastic envelope ratio > 1.00 on ALL held-out seeds 6,7,8,9 (mean +/- 95% CI over 10 stochastic eval seeds), i.e. matches EXP-0006B's strict-envelope clearance on the new contract
gates.secondary: no regression vs EXP-0006B champion (m2_v3_obs_stochastic) per-seed consumer units
gates.behaviour-neutral: the simpler relabel-invariant v3 contract is at least as good as v2 before EXP-0007B automation targets it
